==Problem==
Real numbers <imath>a, b, </imath> and <imath>c</imath> have arithmetic mean <imath>0</imath>. The arithmetic mean of <imath>a^2, b^2, </imath> and <imath>c^2</imath> is <imath>10</imath>. What is the arithmetic mean of <imath>ab, ac, </imath> and <imath>bc</imath>?

<imath>\textbf{(A) } -5 \qquad\textbf{(B) } -\dfrac{10}{3} \qquad\textbf{(C) } -\dfrac{10}{9} \qquad\textbf{(D) } 0 \qquad\textbf{(E) } \dfrac{10}{9}</imath>

==Solution 1==

If <imath>\frac{a+b+c}{3} = 0</imath>, that means <imath>a+b+c=0</imath>, and <imath>(a+b+c)^2=0</imath>. Expanding that gives <cmath>(a+b+c)^2=a^2+b^2+c^2+2ab+2ac+2bc=0</cmath> If <imath>\frac{a^2+b^2+c^2}{3} = 10</imath>, then <imath>a^2+b^2+c^2=30</imath>. Thus, we have <cmath>30 + 2ab + 2ac + 2bc = 0</cmath> Basic arithmetic will give you that <imath>ab + bc + ac = -15</imath>. To find the arithmetic mean, divide that by 3, so <imath>\frac{ab + bc + ac}{3} = \boxed{\textbf{(A) }-5}</imath>

==Solution 3==
Assume that <imath>a = 0</imath> and <imath>b = -c</imath>. Since we know that the arithmetic mean of the three numbers is <imath>10</imath>, this means <imath>a^2+b^2+c^2=30</imath>. Using this equation, <imath>b^{2} + b^{2} = 30</imath>, so <imath>b^2 = 15</imath>. Observe that taking the positive or negative root won't matter as <imath>c</imath> will be the opposite. If we let <imath>b = \sqrt{15}</imath> and <imath>c = -\sqrt{15}</imath>, <imath>ab = 0\times\sqrt{15} = 0</imath>, <imath>ac = 0\times-\sqrt{15} = 0</imath>, and <imath>bc = \sqrt{15}\times-\sqrt{15} = -15</imath>, so <imath>ab+ac+bc=-15</imath>. Doing <imath>\frac{-15}{3}</imath> to get the arithmetic mean will give us <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(A)}\ -5}</imath>.

==Solution 4 (interesting property)==
From the definition of arithmetic means and some simple manipulation, we have <imath>a+b+c=0</imath> and <imath>a^2+b^2+c^2=30</imath>. Let <imath>ab+ac+bc=k</imath>, we have: 

<cmath>k=ab+ac+bc=(a+b)c+ab</cmath>

Substituting <imath>c=-(a+b)</imath> into the expression, we have

<cmath>-c^2+ab=k</cmath>

Adding twice the equation above to <imath>a^2+b^2+c^2=30</imath>, we have:

<cmath>a^2+b^2+c^2-2c^2+2ab=30+2k</cmath>

<cmath>a^2+b^2+2ab-c^2=30+2k</cmath>

<cmath>(a+b)^2-c^2=30+2k</cmath>

<cmath>(a+b+c)(a+b-c)=30+2k</cmath>

But we know that <imath>a+b+c=0</imath>. So <imath>30+2k=0</imath> and <imath>k=-15</imath>. Therefore the arithmetic mean of <imath>ab,ac,bc</imath> is <imath>\frac{k}{3}=-5</imath>. So the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(A)}\ -5}</imath>
